question: You are the agency construction program manager for a large fast food chain in the southwestern United States. The owner has a very tight deadline and a constrained budget to deliver 50 new restaurants by the end of this year, including a new “flagship” store in a major metropolitan area. The entire program will follow the multiple-prime method. During procurement, you notice that there are not enough qualified bidders to complete the program by the owner’s deadline. As the program manager, you recommend:

choices.A: Increasing the program budget to attract more qualified bidders.
choices.B: Lowering the quality requirements to allow more qualified bidders.
choices.C: Phasing delivery to maximize the owner’s ROI.

question: You are the construction manager for a large office facility that is a new construction in a suburban area. The owner is very concerned about maintaining a good relationship with the surrounding community. Which of the following would BEST help the owner achieve this goal?

During the construction phase of a design-bid-build project, the builder hits a natural gas line that will require remediation and will affect the critical path. The builder insists that the natural gas line was unmarked, but the designer says they included the natural gas line in the contract plans and specifications. Which of the following should the construction manager as agent consult FIRST?

You are an at-risk construction manager on a highway expansion project in an area that experiences freezing temperatures each year during November 1st - March 31st. In early October, construction is on-schedule and 50% complete when your subcontractor who mixes and places the concrete suddenly stops coming to work. You are unable to get in contact with them and their absence affects the critical path. Your BEST immediate course of action is to:

choices.A: Submit a change order to delay the project schedule.
choices.B: Submit a claim for the subcontractor’s delay.
choices.D: Hire a new subcontractor to complete the work.

question: You are the agency construction manager on a design-build project. Near the end of the design phase, a new law is passed that has significant impacts on the owner’s industry. The design specifications are not in compliance with this new law. You advise the owner to:

choices.C: Issue a change order to the design-builder.
choices.D: Start construction and implement changes later.

question: An owner who is unfamiliar with construction hires you as the agency construction manager late in the design phase. The owner is renovating their only facility, which is a 10,000 square foot building that is 150 years old. The original drawings from 150 years ago are unavailable. The lead designer recommended a 30% construction contingency, but the owner is very nervous about costs and asks for your recommendation. Your FIRST action is to:

A design-bid-build project is ready to begin the procurement process, but the owner is worried about receiving unbalanced bids. The owner also wants to avoid delays and disputes. Which of the following will BEST accomplish the owner’s goals?

choices.A: If any bids are unbalanced, reject all bids and rebid the project
choices.B: Reject the apparent low bidder if the bid appears unbalanced
choices.C: Allow the apparent low bidder to rebalance if the bid appears unbalanced
choices.D: Include a mobilization payment line item in the bid form

question: You are the construction manager on a design-build project. Construction is 40% complete when the owner submits a change order to increase the project’s scope. What should you do FIRST?

choices.A: Meet with the design-builder to gather the change order pricing
choices.B: Prepare an estimate of the change order’s cost and schedule impacts
choices.D: Meet with the owner to try to dismiss the change order

question: During the design phase, the project team identifies a 25% risk that an important component called Option A would fail to meet one of the owner’s performance requirements. Option A would cost $45,000 to procure and install. The designer points out that there is an Option B for an alternative component from a different manufacturer that has a 5% risk of failure, but Option B would cost $50,000 to procure and install. The owner has not finalized the construction budget and wants your opinion. Your recommendation is to pick:

choices.A: Option A because of the lower lifecycle cost.
choices.B: Option A because of the risk’s higher monetary value.
choices.C: Option B because of the lower lifecycle cost.
choices.D: Option B because of the risk’s lower monetary value.

question: A project team is developing a cash flow schedule. The owner won a grant from an international aid organization to build this project and will need to pay project costs upfront then submit their records to the aid organization for reimbursement. Construction must start within 100 days, but most heavy equipment, materials, and labor will be needed late in the schedule. Which of the following BEST describes the cash flow schedule?
What is the total float (TF) of Activity G?

A project in the post-construction phase experiences a major delay during move-in. The owner’s personnel are unable to enter the facility, shutting down all the owner’s operations for several weeks. Which of the following did the project team MOST LIKELY fail to sufficiently address?

A high-rise hotel is being delivered using multiple-prime contracting. Before construction begins, an electrical contractor asks for more time for an activity that is not on the critical path. The electrician says they cannot start this activity to install floor-mounted electrical fixtures before a different structural contractor installs subfloor. The agency construction manager reviews the project CPM schedule and notices there is no defined relationship between these activities. What is the BEST recommendation to the owner?

The general contractor on a design-bid-build project submits their baseline schedule. After analyzing the plan, the agency construction manager believes it is reasonable and accurately describes the general contractor’s planned work. However, the construction manager makes several comments to help improve the schedule which the general contractor ignores. What should the construction manager do NEXT?

choices.B: Direct the general contractor to change their means and methods
choices.D: Review their own contract with the owner

question: A $60 million airport project is in the construction phase. The project will add 30 new gates to an existing terminal. NOT counting mobilization, construction is scheduled to last 24 months with each gate delivered sequentially in even intervals. After 11 months, 11 gates are now operational. What is the project’s current SPI?

During the design phase on a design-build project, the owner missed an important design review deadline and gave the design-builder approval two working days later than stipulated in the contract. The project ultimately missed its beneficial occupancy deadline by one week. The design-builder has now submitted a claim notification, saying the owner’s design review caused the beneficial occupancy delay. The construction manager acknowledged receipt of the claim. What should the construction manager do NEXT?

A construction management at-risk project with sustainability certification goals is in the construction phase when the construction manager notices that a subcontractor has not properly documented airborne dust prevention. Which of the following would have BEST prevented this?

The owner sends an email to the entire project team to give the formal notice to proceed, but the general contractor does not mobilize for nearly a week and submits a claim, saying the owner did not provide written notice. As the agency construction manager, you recommend that the owner:

You are the program manager on a major office renovation program. Before construction begins, the owner asks you to develop and implement a swing space plan for the owner’s staff who will be displaced. What should you review FIRST?

The contractor submits a proposed progress payment schedule under a unit price contract. The construction manager notices that the contractor’s estimated quantities for an activity late in the schedule are significantly lower than the construction manager’s own estimate. What should the construction manager do NEXT?

choices.A: Recommend the owner make the first payment.
choices.B: Discuss the discrepancy with the contractor.
choices.C: Have the contractor submit a revised schedule.

question: A way for the construction team to test the design’s as-built specifications and quality requirements before construction or a particular construction phase begins that involves a simple model and allows the construction team to perform quality control on the materials, processes, and deliverables is called a 	.

Construction is 75% complete on a design-build project when the design-builder proposes a change order to modify several features that are not yet installed. The design-builder explains that these modifications are necessary to remain on time and on budget. What should the construction manager do FIRST?

choices.D: Advise the owner to reject the change

question: Construction on a luxury hotel is underway when the project team notices that the HVAC system tends to overload the building’s electrical system on warm days. Both systems meet specifications. The building is in a climate that experiences outside temperatures above 80°F (27°C) more than 150 days each year. What could have BEST prevented this?

A project is currently at the schematic design phase. The owner’s representative notifies the entire team of a change that will significantly increase the project’s cost and schedule. The design team incorporates the change and performs QC. Which of the following should the construction manager do NEXT?

choices.A: Have the design team perform a constructability analysis
choices.C: Notify the owner when design is complete

question: During post-construction, the owner asks to meet with the construction manager to assess the project’s quality management. Typically, what document should the construction manager use to create the agenda for this meeting?

You are the agency construction manager on a multiple-prime contracting project. The local municipality has a law which requires all jobsite personnel to wear a P100 respirator when dust or chemical fumes are present. During construction, a mechanical contractor’s team is working with powerful cleaning solvents that emit toxic fumes. The mechanical team are all wearing the correct respirators. However, you notice a worker for a different electrical contractor is performing a separate activity in the same area without a respirator. A spare respirator is not available. Your best immediate response is to:

choices.A: Stop all work and notify the mechanical contractor
choices.B: Stop the electrical worker and notify the mechanical contractor
choices.C: Stop all work and notify the electrical contractor
choices.D: Stop the electrical worker and notify the electrical contractor

question: The general contractor is about to begin a hazardous activity, as defined in the contract documents. The construction manager wants to review the contractor’s plans and procedures for this task. In a typical project, which of the following would help the construction manager the most?

choices.B: The contract between the owner and general contractor
choices.D: The contract between the owner and designer

question: A jobsite accident seriously injures a subcontractor on a design-build project. After the accident investigation, the owner decides that the design-builder’s safety representative performs their duties improperly. The owner wants to remove the safety representative but asks you if this would force the owner to assume responsibility for jobsite safety. As the agency CM, what do you review FIRST?

A project will build a new academic building on a college campus. The jobsite will be fenced off from the rest of the campus but will require the owner to provide a separate staging area for materials. Where would the project team best document this?

A design-bid-build program is in the construction phase. The construction team is at a significant fall risk because the design specifications require the team to do most of their work on a sloped surface several stories off the ground. Per the applicable laws and regulations, the contract documents require all team members to wear a certain fall arresting device, but the general contractor claims it is insufficient and buys additional protective equipment. Typically, who is responsible for the cost of this additional equipment?
Evaluate the expected monetary values for the following risks What should the contingency be for these risks?

During construction, the project team identifies a new risk that has less than a 2% chance of occurring. While the risk would have a moderate cost impact on the project, the schedule and quality impacts cannot be determined. What should the project team do FIRST?

The design team on a design-bid-build project identified a new construction risk. You determine the risk has a monetary value of $800,000 and a 15% chance of occurring. There is an option to transfer this risk which would cost the project $300,000. As the construction manager, what is your recommendation to the owner?

choices.D: Assign the risk to the lead designer

question: You are the construction manager on a project in the pre-design phase. The owner is very concerned about reducing their risk on the project. Which delivery method do you recommend?

You are the construction manager on a project with a scheduled completion date of June 1, 2022. Based on the Monte Carlo simulation output below, what is the project’s earliest expected completion date at the P75 confidence level?

You are the principal of a small but successful construction management firm. Your firm is about six months into a three-year project for an important owner in your market. The owner is your firm’s only client right now. You have a student on staff who is receiving college credit to work in your office and will graduate with a civil engineering degree next month. You want to hire the student permanently because this individual learns quickly and already has a few basic industry certifications, but the owner will not pay for the student’s billable hours until this individual has another year of work experience. What is your response?

choices.A: Write the student a good recommendation letter and wish them luck
choices.B: Offer the student an unpaid internship that will convert to a regular paid position when they gain the experience
choices.C: Offer the student a low “probation” salary that will convert to a regular salary when they gain the experience
choices.D: Offer the student a regular entry-level position and accept the hit to your bottom line the first year

question: You are the agency construction manager on a multiple-prime contracting project in the procurement phase. The private owner is reviewing bids from structural contractors. However, your bid calculations show that the bidders used historical prices for raw materials in their estimates. The current raw material prices are more than 40% higher due to supply chain issues. Your recommendation to the owner is to:

choices.B: Negotiate with the most qualified bidder.
choices.C: Issue an addendum and accept the low bidder.
choices.D: Issue an addendum and re-bid the project

question: Your firm is bidding to offer at-risk construction management services on a project that will include safety management. Your firm has the expertise, liability insurance, and staff to provide safety management, but most of your safety staff are currently involved in a program for a different owner. That program is scheduled to finish a few days before this project, but the program has experienced many delays and you are worried about mobilizing your team in time. What is your response?

choices.A: Submit a bid that assumes all your current staff will be available
choices.B: Submit a bid based on your current staff, but request to delay the project
choices.C: Hire more staff and price them based on their abilities
choices.D: Hire more staff and price them based on your current staff’s abilities

question: You are a senior construction manager who supervises a team of 10 junior construction managers and inspectors. Your team is performing well on a fast-track project, but morale is low. Construction is only 25% complete. How can you BEST manage your team in this situation?

choices.A: Make everyone take a few days of paid vacation
choices.B: Encourage the team to focus on their tasks
choices.C: Analyze the problem and mentor the team
choices.D: Highlight their accomplishments to your supervisor

question: The owner on a multiple-prime contracting project requires each builder to have their own staff training program. The construction management firm has a contract with the owner to provide agency construction management services. In this scenario, who typically manages training for the construction management staff?

choices.C: The appropriate prime builder for each task

question: A local chamber of commerce plans a public-private-partnership project for a disadvantaged urban area. The project is in the conceptual design phase and has a sustainable certification goal, with mixed-use commercial and residential facilities, walkable neighborhoods, and large green spaces. The facilities would use high efficiency lighting, heating, and cooling, and renewable energy sources. The project team wants the city government to help fund the project. Which of the following would BEST help the project team gain financial support from the city council?

choices.A: Identify a LEED goal for the project
choices.B: Evaluate construction’s impact on city residents

question: You are the construction manager on a new office building project with sustainability and resiliency goals that is in the pre-design phase. The building will be in a hot and humid climate about 100 miles (161 kilometers) from the ocean. The town’s historical data from the past 30 years shows that it received one hurricane about every 10 years. What should you do NEXT?

choices.C: Hold a public meeting to get the town’s feedback
choices.D: Hold a meeting to get the end users’ feedback

question: You are the construction manager on a project with sustainable goals. The owner has decided not to pursue a sustainability certification, but still wants the project to meet the standards for two Green Globes. Which of the following is appropriate to manage this project?

choices.A: Include sustainability requirements in the notice to bidders and document performance
choices.B: Focus on the sustainable design, but do not worry about documenting performance
choices.C: Coordinate the project with USGBC and submit documentation
choices.D: Coordinate the project with GBI and submit documentation

question: Which of the following is typically the highest cost in a sustainable facility’s lifecycle?
The owner on a project with very high sustainability goals is concerned that the technology in the current design will be obsolete in 5-10 years. What recommendation do you make to the owner?

choices.A: Plan to update equipment and perform retro-commissioning
choices.B: Use only “state of the art” technology in the design
choices.D: Accept that it will be impossible to further reduce energy use

question: You are an agency CM on a design-bid-build project for a large private owner and construction has begun. The owner has its own quality assurance program and pays its employees significantly more than the market rate. However, the owner is struggling to attract enough qualified inspectors because the project is large and the labor market is tight. Quality is the owner’s highest priority, but the owner is worried that this will cause delays and asks for your advice. What is your best recommendation to the owner?

choices.A: Increase starting pay for the owner’s inspectors
choices.B: Rely on the contractor’s quality assurance and quality control program
choices.C: Invest in automated technology to increase inspectors’ efficiency
choices.D: Install 5G towers near the project jobsite

question: A medium-sized owner in the healthcare industry is starting a new project. The owner wants to receive real-time project updates, but the owner’s IT system has very strict cybersecurity requirements because it also stores patient health records. Your firm is providing construction management at-risk services and has a proprietary system that can provide updates, but the way it is coded does not meet the owner’s security standards. You must resolve this quickly. What do you recommend?

choices.A: Build an API to link your system and the owner’s system to transfer data
choices.B: Build a web portal so the owner’s staff can remotely login to your system
choices.C: Email the owner daily reports from your system
choices.D: Give the owner daily reports over the telephone

question: The design team is using a 4D BIM model to develop the project’s specifications. Why would the team use a 4D model?

The program owner needs to monitor the real-time status of all the systems in their facilities, such as smoke detectors, alarms, access control, lighting, HVAC, etc., from a central location. Which of the following concepts or tools would best help the owner accomplish this?

You are the construction manager on an airport runway project. This runway must have a slope or gradient of 1.0% down (-1.0%). You require the survey team to take SONAR, RADAR, and LiDAR readings of the project site and use them to build a 3D model. Which of the following concepts or tools MUST the survey team use to accomplish this?
